What i actually need is

(a1, b1) < (a2, b2) ↔ a1 < a2 ∨ (a1 ≐ a2) ∧ (b1 < b2)

This is well behaved under the following compatibility assumption in the first component:
"C1 ≐ D1 → C2 ≐ D2 → C1 < C2 → D1 < D2"
where ≐ is some Equivalence, and < a strict order on the first component.

Is there maybe a class for the compatibility assumption?
do you want to use some specific equivalence?
Later yes, but for now it needs to be axiomatized
There may be multiple (equivalences,order) pairs which work for my case
isn't this just lexicographic < on the docs#Antisymmetrization of an order?
the version of the lexicographic product order in mathlib isn't very nice with preorders

Lets call the first component type F and the second L.
Do i understand correctly that you mean to construct the Prod.Lex on (Quot F) × L and then lift this to an order on F × L?
